messages:
sara-sales: Hi team — we're ramping an enterprise POC for NimbusHealth (Private deployment). They have a strict egress allowlist requirement. Two asks: (1) who owns provisioning the outbound static IPs / BYOIP mapping for the POC, and (2) what's the pricing delta if they require static EIPs per connector vs using our shared egress? cc @matt-netops @devon-arch

matt-netops: @sara-sales short version: customer can provide their egress IPs (preferred) or we can allocate EIPs in their account when needed. For interface endpoints (VPCE) we normally rely on AWS-managed addresses, but for src-ip preservation or dedicated NAT flows customers often want static EIPs. Pricing-wise it's mostly an infra/add-on: per-connector static EIP surcharge + possible monthly reserved-capacity delta. I'll pull exact numbers. :thinking_face:

devon-arch: Ownership is usually three-way: customer provides if they want absolute src-ip preservation; otherwise we can host egress from their VPC via a managed NAT/proxy. For Private deployments, we can also provide a list of outbound prefixes (ASN/prefix list) for firewall allowlisting. For a POC I'd recommend customer-provided IPs to avoid churn.

jen-engineer: Adding the minimal firewall snippet we share with customers — basically allow outbound 443 to our endpoints and optionally the VPCE whitelist: 
```
# Customer firewall example (AWS on-prem / corp FW)
allow tcp 443 to 52.23.12.0/24    # example Redwood hosted egress pool
allow tcp 443 to vpce-xxxxxxxx.vpce-svc.amazonaws.com  # VPCE FQDN
# If TLS inspect required, allow hostnames: api.redwood.inference, telemetry.redwood.inference
```

sara-sales: Good. Also the security team asked: if the firewall accidentally blocks traffic during a rollout, do we have any circuit-breaker or fallback so patient systems don't fail catastrophically? Customer worries about a hard outage during canary.

ops-oncall-bot: Incident playbook note: for Private connector failure due to egress blockage we attempt automatic fallback to in-region Redwood dedicated backend when policy allows. If fallback disallowed by customer policy, errors will surface. Recommend canary 5-10% with an automatic rollback/fallback window and an alert to oncall.

matt-netops: Important gotcha — DNS and SNI. If the customer uses Private DNS and VPCEs, their firewall needs to permit the VPCE hostnames or the AWS-managed IP ranges. If they're doing TLS inspection, they must ensure SNI passthrough for our hostnames or add the hostnames to allowed list. IPs can change with provider-managed endpoints, so hostnames are safer.

sara-sales: Timeline: Nimbus wants the POC next week. They need the final allowlist + a clarified quote for static-eip option by EOD Friday. Who can own that deliverable?

devon-arch: I'll own the allowlist checklist and provide a CSV with two columns: "type" (IP or FQDN) and "value". I'll include recommended canary config and fallback policy. ETA: Thursday afternoon.

sara-sales: amazing, thanks 🙏

matt-netops: For pricing: if they opt for per-connector static EIPs we have a one-time onboarding fee + monthly surcharge to cover reserved capacity and monitoring. I'll DM finance and paste the numbers here once confirmed.

jen-engineer: Also need the customer CIDR to run quick reachability checks from our staging VPC and to validate source NAT behavior.

sara-sales: CIDR is 10.10.0.0/16 — sharing with devon/matt.

matt-netops: Quick reachability test I usually give customers: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.inference/healthz --resolve api.redwood.inference:443:52.23.12.8
```
This forces name resolution to an example egress IP for quick local FW checks.

sara-sales: Perfect. I'll send the initial ask to Nimbus and loop back when devon posts the CSV. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
